c.tagline: Sunny riverside Queensland capital of subtropical, outdoor ease.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered (Yellow Cabs and Black & White Cabs are the main operators); a booking fee applies for phone or app bookings and airport pickups add a surcharge.

emergency.note: 000 is the primary emergency number; 112 also works from any mobile and 106 is the text-based line for the deaf or speech-impaired.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Fortitude Valley's nightlife strip can get aggressive with intoxicated crowds after midnight.

hood_desc: The riverside city centre packed with Queen Street Mall, Queen's Wharf, City Botanic Gardens, Howard Smith Wharves, and easy access to trains, buses, and ferries; the convenient walkable base for first-timers.

A relaxed cultural and family precinct on the south bank of the river, home to South Bank Parklands, the Streets Beach lagoon, GOMA and the Queensland Cultural Centre, plus riverfront dining just across from the CBD.

Australia's first designated entertainment precinct, buzzing with live-music venues, bars and clubs, multicultural restaurants, and the designer boutiques and fine dining of James Street; the place to go out.
A trendy, bohemian inner-city village of leafy streets, indie cafes, street art, vintage shops, and Saturday markets along Boundary Street; suits younger travellers wanting an arty, local vibe.

An upscale, leafy riverside suburb known for stylish shopping, boutique cinema and theatre, weekend markets, New Farm Park, and classic cafes; a quieter, more residential base with lovely riverside walks.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink across Brisbane.

transit.hours: Trains run roughly 5:00am to midnight; buses, the Brisbane Metro, and CityCat/CityHopper ferries run similar daytime-to-late-evening hours, with reduced weekend and late-night frequency.
transit.note: One TransLink network across South East Queensland covers trains, buses, the Brisbane Metro, and river ferries; the free CityHopper ferry and free City Loop / Spring Hill Loop buses are handy in the centre.
transit.pay: Tap on and off with a go card (being replaced by the new Smart Ticketing 'Translink card') or a contactless Visa, Mastercard, or Amex card or phone. Since 2024 every journey is a flat 50-cent fare, regardless of distance or mode, with transfers within the journey included.

transit.m: Airtrain to city stations (~20 min, every 15-30 min)
TransLink route 590 bus (50-cent flat fare, longer)

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up or leaving around 10% for excellent service at restaurants is appreciated but never obligatory.

food.name: Barramundi
food.desc: Queensland's flagship fish, thick-filleted and mild, usually pan-seared skin-side down or grilled and served with local greens and citrus.

places.name: OTTO Brisbane
places.note: Riverfront fine dining that treats Queensland fish simply and precisely.

places.name: Stokehouse Q
places.note: River-view restaurant in the parklands, long a Brisbane special-occasion seafood pick.

places.name: Riverbar & Kitchen
places.note: Casual all-day riverside spot; grilled fish, beer and Story Bridge views.

food.name: Moreton Bay bugs
food.desc: Flat slipper lobsters from Moreton Bay with sweet, firm tails; split and grilled with garlic butter or served cold with lemon.

places.name: Stokehouse Q
places.note: Puts local bugs and reef fish at the centre of the menu; book the river side.

places.name: Jellyfish Restaurant
places.note: Long-established seafood room specialising in Queensland shellfish and crab.

places.name: Rico's Bar & Dining
places.note: Tapas-style plates including a signature Moreton Bay bug brioche roll.

food.name: Queensland mud crab
food.desc: Heavy-clawed mangrove crab, steamed or wok-tossed with chilli, ginger and garlic; messy, expensive and worth it.

places.name: Jellyfish Restaurant
places.note: Reliable source for whole mud crab cooked to order by the kilo.

places.name: Stokehouse Q
places.note: Seasonal crab dishes plus a raw bar of Queensland oysters and prawns.

places.name: Morgan's Seafood Market
places.note: Working seafood market north of the city; buy live crab or eat cooked on site.

food.name: Aussie meat pie
food.desc: Hand-sized shortcrust and puff pastry pie of minced beef in thick gravy, eaten with a squeeze of tomato sauce, often as a footy or servo lunch.

places.name: James Street Bakery
places.note: Handmade pies with big chunks of beef and proper gravy; also good sausage rolls.

places.name: Carindale Bakery
places.note: Suburban bakery with a devoted local following for its classic beef pies.

places.name: Yatala Pie Shop
places.note: Roadside institution since 1880; the traditional pie stop on the Gold Coast run.

food.name: Lamington
food.desc: Squares of butter sponge dipped in thin chocolate icing and rolled in desiccated coconut; invented in Queensland and often split with cream and jam.

places.name: Jocelyn's Provisions
places.note: Brisbane institution; moist orange-scented sponge, raspberry and hundreds-and-thousands versions.

places.name: Flour and Chocolate Patisserie
places.note: Cult neighbourhood patisserie; go early before the pastry case empties.

places.name: The Lord Lamington
places.note: Lamington specialist with a terminal outlet, handy for a last-minute box.

food.name: Char-grilled Queensland steak
food.desc: Grain-fed rump or scotch fillet from Queensland cattle country, cooked over coals and served with chips, salad and a help-yourself sauce bar.

places.name: Breakfast Creek Hotel
places.note: 1889 pub whose coal-grilled rump is a Brisbane rite of passage; get a beer off the wood.

places.name: Norman Hotel
places.note: Self-styled 'Brisbane's worst vegetarian restaurant'; big steaks near the Gabba.

places.name: Cha Cha Char
places.note: Upmarket wine-bar grill known for aged and single-origin Queensland beef.

food.name: Queensland craft beer and XXXX
food.desc: XXXX is the state's century-old lager; the modern scene runs to hazy pale ales and crisp lagers poured in Brisbane warehouse taprooms.

places.name: XXXX Brewery Tours & Ale House
places.note: Tour Queensland's most famous brewery and drink it fresh at the source.

places.name: Green Beacon Brewing Co.
places.note: Popular riverside warehouse taproom; Windjammer IPA and fresh seafood snacks.

places.name: Newstead Brewing Co.
places.note: Brewpub with a big beer garden and a rotating tap list of local brews.

food.name: Flat white coffee
food.desc: Australia's espresso staple: a double shot under steamed milk with a thin layer of microfoam. Brisbane cafes take the roast seriously.

places.name: John Mills Himself
places.note: Tiny heritage laneway cafe that helped start Brisbane's specialty coffee scene.

places.name: Coffee Anthology
places.note: Rotating guest roasters and consistently well-pulled shots in the city centre.

places.name: Sourced Grocer
places.note: Grocer-cafe in a converted warehouse; strong coffee and a good breakfast menu.

landmarks: Story Bridge
Brisbane's most recognizable steel cantilever bridge, spectacularly lit at night and offering thrilling climb tours over the river.
South Bank Parklands (Streets Beach)
A lush riverside precinct featuring Australia's only inner-city man-made beach, framed by palm trees and skyline views.
Mount Coot-tha Lookout
The best vantage point for a sweeping panorama of the entire Brisbane skyline against the Glass House Mountains backdrop.
Brisbane City Hall
A grand 1930 sandstone landmark with a soaring clock tower, the historic civic heart of the city and a striking piece of neoclassical architecture.
Kangaroo Point Cliffs
Dramatic riverside sandstone cliffs popular with rock climbers, offering some of the finest photographic views of the CBD skyline.
Howard Smith Wharves
A revitalized riverside precinct beneath the Story Bridge, blending heritage warehouses, dining, and a striking zigzag boardwalk against the cliff face.
Gallery of Modern Art (GOMA)
Australia's largest contemporary art gallery, a bold architectural statement on the South Bank riverfront housing cutting-edge exhibitions.
Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary
The world's first and largest koala sanctuary, where visitors can cuddle koalas and see kangaroos in a beloved Brisbane institution.
Wheel of Brisbane
A 60-metre observation wheel at South Bank offering panoramic river and skyline views, an eye-catching feature of the city's night skyline.
City Botanic Gardens
Lush riverside gardens dating to 1855, featuring fig-lined avenues, tropical plants, and postcard views of the Story Bridge and skyline.

dom.op: Queensland Rail Travel (Spirit of Queensland, Tilt Train, Spirit of the Outback, Westlander)

train.note: Australia has no cross-border railways, so every train from Brisbane is domestic; long-distance services use Roma Street station on the edge of the CBD, while suburban and airport trains also call at Central. Queensland Rail Travel's Spirit of Queensland runs five times a week up the coast to Cairns in about 25 hours with lie-flat RailBed seats, and the Tilt Train, Spirit of the Outback and Westlander head to Rockhampton, Longreach and Charleville. NSW TrainLink's daily XPT to Sydney takes roughly 14 hours - slower than flying but cheap and scenic through the Northern Rivers. Journey Beyond's all-inclusive Great Southern tourist train links Brisbane and Adelaide only in the December-February season and sells out months ahead.

bus.note: There are no international coaches from Australia; Greyhound Australia (https://www.greyhound.com.au/) is the main long-distance network, running north up the Bruce Highway to Hervey Bay, Airlie Beach, Townsville and Cairns and south to Byron Bay and Sydney, plus inland routes to Toowoomba and Roma. Coaches use the Roma Street terminal precinct beside the railway station, a 15-minute walk from Queen Street Mall. Tickets are cheapest booked online in advance; Brisbane to Sydney is around 16-17 hours and Brisbane to Cairns about 29 hours, so most travellers break the trip. Local and regional buses across South East Queensland are covered by Translink (https://translink.com.au/).

intl.to: Moreton Island (Australia) - vehicle and passenger ferry from the Port of Brisbane at Lytton, ~25 km east of the CBD
Tangalooma, Moreton Island (Australia) - launch from Holt Street Wharf, Pinkenba
North Stradbroke Island (Australia) - vehicle ferry and water taxi from Cleveland, ~45 min south-east by train and bus

ferry.note: Brisbane has no international or interstate passenger ferries; all sailings are short hops into Moreton Bay. MICAT's vehicle barge takes about 75-90 minutes to Tangalooma Wrecks and vehicles must be booked well ahead, especially in school holidays, while the Tangalooma resort launch from Pinkenba is passenger-only and takes about 75 minutes. Ferries to North Stradbroke Island leave from Cleveland, reachable by suburban train, with the water taxi taking about 25 minutes and the vehicle ferry about 45. Within the city, Translink's CityCat and Kitty Cat river ferries run frequently along the Brisbane River on a normal public transport fare.

half.name: Gold Coast
half.blurb: Beach resort strip of high-rise towers, surf breaks and theme parks about an hour south of Brisbane.

half.name: Sunshine Coast
half.blurb: Laid-back beach region north of Brisbane with hinterland rainforest towns and the Glass House Mountains.

half.name: Springbrook National Park
half.blurb: Rainforest plateau of waterfalls and glow-worm caves in the Gold Coast hinterland, part of a Gondwana rainforest reserve.

half.name: Moreton Island
half.blurb: Mostly-undeveloped sand island reached by ferry from Brisbane, known for shipwreck snorkeling, dingoes and towering coastal sand dunes.
